flags: Partial overview history: no cache page explains Route 218’s construction, promoters or designation rationale. Used supported Caledon protection history and a shorter overview rather than inventing road history or an agency evaluation.

The byway-list cache lacks its table. Current two-piece designation limits and material’s March 20, 1997 date are unverified and omitted; the route article supports only that most of Route 218 in King George County is a Virginia Byway. Driving sequence describes the numbered highway, not verified designation boundaries.

Passapatanzy history and tribal tradition are available only through a secondary encyclopedia, with no cached Patawomeck or Mattaponi source. Retained named tradition as tradition; narrowed current capture assertion to the plan actually described by the cache. Community review warranted before publication.
Dropped the current Alexander brothers/founders of Alexandria/1659 plantation claim despite its presence in 16.txt: its compressed chronology is not corroborated by another cached historical source.

Fairview Beach is intentionally short: the cache supports geography but little place history and no public beach access. Caledon’s kind changed to separate excursion; the highway skirts the park, and no roadside view of old-growth trees or eagles is promised.

Caledon remains below the normal moment length because its single short source provides little reliable detail beyond acreage, protection and habitat. Fairview Beach likewise stays short; neither is padded with census statistics.
